name: Enterprise Dataset and Data Contract
constraints: WM-DAT-001 is the sole authority for dataset, dataset-version and distribution identity; EM-DAT-01 creates no aggregate or runtime identity.
WM-DAT-004 is the sole authority for schema and contract-version identity, compatibility assessment and producer-consumer obligations.
Every released dataset version has a stable dataset identifier and a distinct version-scoped identifier.
Released dataset-version and distribution assertions are immutable: changed bytes require a new distribution identity or a successor dataset version, and existing fixity is never overwritten.
Every published distribution carries a named digest algorithm and digest value, or references a signed manifest that itself carries that digest.
Every governed dataset version has append-only, timestamped conformance assertions that pin an exact WM-DAT-004 contract version and record conformance status.

At one conformance assertion time all distributions of a dataset version bind the same contract version; later assertions preserve history, so dataset and contract versions may advance independently without mutable latest links.
Every compatibility outcome names its baseline dataset and contract version set; transitive modes name every evaluated predecessor.
Compatibility mode NONE requires a recorded accountable exception and never yields an implicit compatible outcome.
The published compatibility outcome covers structural, governed semantic and value-domain changes plus any declared content-compatibility assessment.
Dataset breaking-change status is derived solely from that scoped published compatibility outcome and is never asserted independently.
Consumer scope and an explicit change-notice path are declared; channel, notice duration and service levels remain deployment policy.
Issuing a successor dataset version records predecessor and provenance assertions without absorbing the full lineage graph.
Designated critical data elements bind authoritative governed-term and value-domain versions; designation policy remains external.
A catalogue record describes a dataset and never replaces the dataset or its version identity.
Dataset-level quality evidence is a reference or summary only; EM-DAT-04 and its base authorities own quality rules, metrics, observations and assessment runs.
An ODCS dataProduct element is an imported reference to the WM-DAT-008 and EM-DAT-02 data-product authority, never a second product or dataset identity.
Pipeline and deep-lineage graphs remain external masters; this profile requires only predecessor and provenance references.
PID scheme, licence catalogue, consumer-registration enforcement, freshness targets and ODCS dialect selection beyond an exact version pin remain deployment policy.
DatasetSchemaContract and other fused roots are forbidden; the conformance binding remains a WM-DAT-001 dataset-version facet referencing WM-DAT-004.
holds: WM-DAT-001 and WM-DAT-004 remain reviewable drafts with publishableCanonical false.
DataCite source-version consistency and live source pinning remain unresolved.
ODCS version pinning and the dataProduct deprecation contradiction remain unresolved.
The single frozen audit found released-version immutability and breaking-source scope defects; candidate.3 repairs both without an audit rerun.
This candidate is a non-canonical reviewable profile only.
